\subsection*{算法2：估计图中完美匹配的数量}

\textbf{输入：} $G = (V, E)$ 是一个无向图，具有 $n = |V|$ 个顶点，且存在一个完美匹配

\textbf{输出：} $G$ 中完美匹配数量的估计值 $X_G$

\begin{enumerate}
    \item $X_G \leftarrow 1$
    \item $G^{(1)} \leftarrow G$
    \item \textbf{for} $i = 1$ 到 $n$，步长为 $2$ \textbf{do}
    \item \quad 令 $A^{(i)}$ 为 $G^{(i)}$ 的邻接矩阵。
    \item \quad 过滤掉 $A^{(i)}$ 中那些在对应于 $A^{(i)}$ 的二部图中无法放入完美匹配的条目，并令 $G^{(i)}$ 对应于 $A^{(i)}$ 的图
    \item \quad $[R^{(i)}] \leftarrow \text{缩放}(A^{(i)})$
    \item \quad 令 $T = \{j : a^{(i)}_{1,j} \neq 0 \text{ 且 } G^{(i)} - \{v_1, v_j\} \text{ 存在一个完美匹配}\}$
    \item \quad 使用概率密度函数从 $T$ 中随机选择一个非零列 $j$
    \[
    p_k = \frac{s_{1,k}}{\sum_{t \in T} s_{1,t}}, \quad \text{对于所有 } k \in T \text{ 中的非零 } a^{(i)}_{1,k}
    \]
    其中 $s_{t,k} = r^{(i)}_t \cdot r^{(i)}_k$ 是缩放矩阵 $S = R^{(i)} A^{(i)} R^{(i)}$ 中的对应条目
    \item \quad $X_G \leftarrow X_G / p_j$
    \item \quad $G^{(i+1)} \leftarrow G^{(i)} - \{v_1, v_j\}$ \quad $\triangleright$ 从 $G^{(i)}$ 中删除顶点 $v_1$ 和 $v_j$ 得到 $G^{(i+1)}$
\end{enumerate}

其中 $T = \{j : a^{(i)}_{1,j} \neq 0 \text{ 且 } G^{(i)} - \{v_1, v_j\} \text{ 存在一个完美匹配}\}$，$s_{1,t} = r^{(i)}_1 \cdot r^{(i)}_t$，且 $0 < \sum_{t \in T} s_{1,t} \leq 1$。因此，在算法2的第8行，$p_k \geq r^{(i)}_1 \cdot r^{(i)}_k$。

通过使用类似于定理1的证明，我们可以得到关于算法2返回的估计量期望值的以下结论。

\textbf{定理5.} 令 $X_G$ 为算法2返回的随机变量。则 $\mathbb{E}[X_G] = M(G)$，其中 $M(G)$ 表示图 $G$ 中完美匹配的数量。

\textbf{证明.} 我们通过归纳法证明该论断。作为基础情况，考虑 $n = 2$，且论断成立，此时邻接矩阵为 $A = [[0, 1], [1, 0]]$。假设归纳假设对 $n-2$ 成立。令 $G_{ij}$ 是通过从 $G$ 中移除顶点 $v_i$ 和 $v_j$ 得到的图，这对应于删除 $G$ 的邻接矩阵的第 $i$ 行和第 $j$ 列，从而形成 $G_{ij}$ 的 $(n-2) \times (n-2)$ 邻接矩阵 $A_{ij}$。我们有：

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[X_G] &= \sum_{j: a_{1,j} \neq 0} p_j \cdot (1/p_j) \cdot \mathbb{E}[X_{G_{ij}}] \\
&= \sum_{j: a_{1,j} \neq 0} \mathbb{E}[X_{G_{ij}}] \\
&= \sum_{j: a_{1,j} \neq 0} M(G_{ij}) \quad (\text{由归纳假设}) \\
&= M(G)
\end{aligned}
\]

\subsection*{5.1 过滤冗余边}

在无向图情形中，一个复杂之处在于，仅使用$A$的Dulmage-Mendelsohn分解不足以消除不属于任何完美匹配的边。我们通过以下事实来证明这一点。

\textbf{事实7.} 设$G$为一个无向图，$A$为$G$的$n \times n$邻接矩阵。则$\operatorname{Per}(A)$大于或等于$M(G)$。

\textbf{证明.} 在$M(G)=0$的情况下，该事实显然成立。因此，下面我们假设$M(G)>0$。设$G'$为从$A$得到的具有$2n$个顶点的二分图。那么，对于$G=(V,E)$中的每个完美匹配，在$G'=(V',E')$中存在一个对应的完美匹配。设$\{(u_1,u_2),\dots,(u_{n-1},u_n)\}$是$G$中的一个完美匹配，其中对于$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$，有$u_i\in V$。将二分图$G'$的第一部分和第二部分中的顶点分别记为$v_i$和$w_i$，其中对于$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$，有$v_i\in V'$且$w_i\in V'$。

由于对于$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$，边$(u_i,u_{i+1})$在匹配中，因此它在$G$中。所以$a_{i,i+1}=a_{i+1,i}=1$是$A$中的非零元。因此，在二分图$G'$中，我们有边$(v_i,w_{i+1})\in E'$和$(v_{i+1},w_i)\in E'$。从这些边出发，可以在$G'$中构造一个完美匹配。

因此，对于$G$中的每个匹配，可以在$G'$中构造一个完美匹配，且$G'$中完美匹配的数量等于$\operatorname{Per}(A)$。因此，$\operatorname{Per}(A)$至少与$M(G)$一样大。

上述事实表明，在$A$的Dulmage-Mendelsohn分解中，任何非对角边都不能属于$G$中的完美匹配，但这并不能帮助我们消除那些可能不属于这种对称匹配$(v_i,w_j)$和$(w_j,v_i)$的边。这些边可以通过使用计算最大匹配的精确算法来清除，以检测选择其中一条边是否会导致剩余顶点存在完美匹配。读者可能会问，是否可以使用Gallai-Edmonds分解\cite{20, 第3.2节}，该分解将Dulmage-Mendelsohn分解部分扩展到无向图。如果图中没有完美匹配，这种分解可用于找到完美可匹配子图和奇分支。但对于具有完美匹配的图，它无法提供对我们目标有用的信息，而二分图的Dulmage-Mendelsohn分解则能指出哪些边不能放入完美匹配中。

\textbf{7 结论}

我们提出了一种用于近似无向图中永久和计数完美匹配的技术。我们的方法使用矩阵缩放来随机采样图的一个完美匹配。在算法的每一步，我们选择一个顶点，并随机将其与一个邻居匹配。我们进行选择所依据的概率是通过将图的邻接矩阵缩放为双随机形式，并检查与给定顶点邻居对应的条目而获得的。在算法结束时，得到一个估计值$X$。

\[
g_B(d,d) \leq g_B(r',r')
\]
即
\[
d^{\mathsf{T}} B d - 2 \cdot \sum_{z=1}^{n-2} \ln d_z \leq r'^{\mathsf{T}} B r' - 2 \cdot \sum_{z=1}^{n-2} \ln r'_z.
\]
我们有
\[
d^{\mathsf{T}} B d = n-2
\]
且
\[
r'^{\mathsf{T}} B r' \leq n-4 + 2 \cdot r_1 \cdot r_j.
\]
因此
\[
n-2 - 2 \cdot \sum_{z=1}^{n-2} \ln d_z \leq n-2-2 + 2 \cdot (r_1 \cdot r_j) - 2 \cdot \sum_{z=1}^{n-2} \ln r'_z,
\]
即
\[
-\sum_{z=1}^{n-2} \ln d_z \leq -1 + r_1 \cdot r_j - \sum_{z=1}^{n-2} \ln r'_z.
\]
然后对两边取指数即可得到结果。

根据归纳假设，其中$D$和$E$对$A_{1j}$进行缩放，$k(j)$是与$A_{1j}$相关的向量，且$v(j) = \|k(j)\|$。因此，

Scaling matrices and counting
the perfect matchings in graphs


Fanny Dufoss´e∗, Kamer Kaya†, Ioannis Panagiotas‡, and Bora U¸car§

December 28, 2021



Abstract
Weinvestigateefficientrandomizedmethodsforapproximatingthenumberofperfectmatch-
ings in bipartite graphs and general undirected graphs. Our approach is based on assigning
probabilities to edges, randomly selecting an edge to be in a perfect matching, and discard-
ing edges that cannot be put in a perfect matching. The probabilities are chosen according
to the entries in the doubly stochastically scaled version of the adjacency matrix of the given
graph. The experimental analysis on random and real-life graphs shows improvements in the
approximation over previous and similar methods from the literature.
Keywords: permanent, perfect matching, doubly stochastic matrix.


1  Introduction

We investigate efficient randomized methods for approximating the number of perfect matchings in
bipartite graphs and general undirected graphs. Our main tool is a sparse matrix scaling algorithm
which we apply to the adjacency matrix of the given graph (bipartite or general) to assign prob-
abilities to the edges and base random choices to these probabilities. Previously, we have shown
that such scaling algorithms are useful in approximating the maximum cardinality of matchings in
bipartite graphs [6] and general undirected graphs [7].
A given bipartite graph with n vertices on both sides has an n × n unsymmetric adjacency
matrix A, where a = 1 if the vertex i on the first part and the vertex j on the second part are

Approximating the permanent is a well-studied problem. Valiant [26] showed the problem to
be #P-Complete. Jerrum et al. [13] discuss an approach using Markov Chains which can provide
an (1 + ε)-approximation for the permanent in fully polynomial time, with O˜(n10) complexity.
Their Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach makes use of the underlying graph being
bipartite, and the techniques cannot be generalized easily to the general graph case. Sˇtefankovic
et al. [24] take the MCMC approach and highlight the difficulties that arise. They also propose a
Markov Chain for efficiently estimating the number of perfect matchings in graphs from a special
class. Gurvits and Samorodnitsky [11] and Linial et al. [19] have used matrix scaling and proposed
deterministic approximations with exponential guarantees (2n and en respectively).
Rasmussen [22] proposes a practicallyefficient wayof estimatingthe permanent ofa 0-1matrix,
or the number of perfect matchings in bipartite graphs. This initial work is followed by a series of
others [2, 9, 10]. Rasmussen’s iterative algorithm uniformly and randomly chooses a nonzero from
the first row in the matrix at hand and discards the first row and the column of the chosen nonzero.
Thisstepisrepeateduntilthewholematrixisconsumedorthereisanemptyrowremaining. Inthe
former case, an estimate of a nonzero value is returned which is based on the number of nonzeros
of the first rows at each step; in the latter case zero is returned as an estimate.
We investigate an improvement of Rasmussen’s original approach in which edges are selected
non-uniformlybasedonamatrixscalingmethod,whichscalesamatrixtobedoublystochastic. We
provide an analysis of the stated approach by meticulously tracking the steps taken. The analysis

upper bounds the number of repetitions we must run to have quality guarantees on the estimated
permanent. To the best of our knowledge, for scaling-based permanent estimation, this work
presents the most thorough analysis in the literature with computable bounds. These ideas are also
extended to counting the number of perfect matchings in graphs. On the practical side, we present
an extensive set of experiments on a variety of random, constructed, and real-life instances, some
with known and others with unknown number of perfect matchings. Our experiments show that
the scaling-based selection mechanism exhibits a significantly better performance on all instances
comparedtotheknownmethods. Furthermore,thepracticalperformanceofouralgorithmseemsto
be even superior to the expected performance derived from our theoretical analysis, which implies
that there exist further avenues to explore.
The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 introduces the notation and the back-
ground on scaling and the permanent, and Section 3 discusses related work in detail. Section 4
introduces the proposed approach and presents the pseudocode of the main algorithm for bipartite
graphs. The extension to the general, undirected case is presented in Section 5. Section 6 presents
the experimental results and a comparison with existing algorithms. Section 7 concludes the paper.

3  Related  work
Rasmussen [22] proposes a practically efficient randomized approach for estimating the permanent
of a 0-1 matrix, or for counting perfect matchings in bipartite graphs. Rasmussen’s algorithm
visits the first row of a matrix and among the nonzeros, chooses one with uniform probability. The
first row and the column of the selected nonzero are then removed from the matrix and a smaller
matrix is obtained. This process is repeated until either there exists an empty row, in which case
zero is returned; or all rows of the original matrix were able to choose a column, in which case a
nonzero estimator of the permanent X is returned. This estimator is the product of the number
Ra
ofnonzerosofthefirstrowsforwhichtherandomselectionsaredone. WhileRasmussen’sestimator
returns zero in most of the cases, it is an unbiased estimator, and its expected value is equal to

6.2 Experiments on general, undirected graphs

We examine the performance of the estimators on five undirected graphs obtained from matrices
available in the SuiteSparse Matrix Collection. After downloading the matrices, we made them
pattern-wise symmetric by adding all missing symmetric entries. Furthermore, we discarded the
values in the diagonal and set all remaining nonzero values to one so that the resulting matrix is
the adjacency matrix of an undirected graph. The properties of the resulting graphs are presented
in Table 3.
As discussed in Section 5.1, getting rid of the entries that do not belong to any perfect match-
ing is a more time consuming procedure than its equivalent for bipartite graphs. As Fu¨rer and
Kasiviswanathan [10] discard all edges that cannot be put into a perfect matching from the graph
in the original description of Greedy, we implemented this cleaning for Greedy. For the extension
of Rasmussen’s approach for undirected graphs, first, we select a row and then we remove any of
its entries that do not participate in any perfect matching, so that we always end up with a valid
perfect matching. For the proposed scaling-based algorithm we opted to test the following two
alternatives:

1. The results labeled Scaling in the figures correspond to Algorithm 2. In this version, the
Dulmage-Mendelsohn decomposition is used to ensure that the matrix has total support.
Then we cleaned only the entries from the selected row.

2. The results labeled with Clear-Scaling are obtained by discarding all edges that are not
part of some perfect matching, using first the Dulmage-Mendelsohn decomposition, and then
by exhaustively testing the remaining edges (due to Fact 7, the resulting matrix has total
support). Then we proceed to scale the matrix to obtain the scaling matrix R and do the
appropriate selections. This corresponds to the cleaning performed in Greedy.
We do not know the actual number of perfect matchings on these graphs. As in the previous
subsection, we plot the distribution (in logarithmic scale) of the results for 1000 trials. The results
are presented in Figure 5. We observe that the two scaling-based alternatives have similar curves,
and there does not seem to be an advantage in applying the more expensive method of extensive
cleaning. In addition, we observe that our approach seems to minimize the variance in respect to
the other alternatives by providing a closer range of reported values.

We have proposed a technique for approximating the permanent and counting perfect matchings
in undirected graphs. Our approach uses matrix scaling in order to sample randomly a perfect
matching of the graph. At each step of the algorithm, we select a vertex and match it randomly
with one of its neighbors. The probabilities upon which we base the selection are obtained by
scaling the adjacency matrix of the graph into a doubly stochastic form and examining the entries
that correspond to the neighbors of the given vertex. At the end of the algorithm an estimate X is

\documentclass[12pt]{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage{xeCJK}

\begin{document}

% ===== 第 3 页 =====
近似计算积和式是一个被广泛研究的问题。Valiant \cite{26} 证明了该问题是 \#P-完全的。Jerrum 等人 \cite{13} 讨论了一种使用马尔可夫链的方法，该方法能够在完全多项式时间内提供积和式的 $(1 + \varepsilon)$-近似，其复杂度为 $\tilde{O}(n^{10})$。他们的马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛 (MCMC) 方法利用了底层图是二分图这一性质，且该技术难以轻易推广到一般图的情况。Štefankovič 等人 \cite{24} 采用了 MCMC 方法并指出了其中出现的困难。他们还提出了一种马尔可夫链，用于高效估计特殊类别图中完美匹配的数量。Gurvits 和 Samorodnitsky \cite{11} 以及 Linial 等人 \cite{19} 使用了矩阵缩放方法，并提出了具有指数级保证的确定性近似（分别为 $2^{n}$ 和 $e^{n}$）。

Rasmussen \cite{22} 提出了一种实际高效的方法来估计 0-1 矩阵的积和式，或二分图中完美匹配的数量。这项开创性工作之后又有一系列后续研究 \cite{2,9,10}。Rasmussen 的迭代算法均匀且随机地从当前矩阵的第一行中选择一个非零元素，然后删除该非零元素所在的第一行和列。重复此步骤，直到整个矩阵被消耗完或剩余一个空行。在前一种情况下，基于每一步第一行中非零元素的数量返回一个非零值的估计；在后一种情况下，返回零作为估计值。

我们研究了 Rasmussen 原始方法的一种改进，其中边的选择基于一种矩阵缩放方法而非均匀选择，该方法将矩阵缩放为双随机矩阵。我们通过细致追踪所采取的步骤，对所述方法进行了分析。该分析给出了我们必须运行的重复次数的上界，以确保对估计的积和式有质量保证。据我们所知，对于基于缩放的积和式估计，本文提出了文献中最详尽的分析，并给出了可计算的界。这些思想也被扩展到计算图中完美匹配的数量。在实际方面，我们在各种随机、构造和现实实例上进行了一系列广泛的实验，其中一些实例的完美匹配数量已知，另一些则未知。我们的实验表明，与已知方法相比，基于缩放的选取机制在所有实例上都表现出显著更优的性能。此外，我们算法的实际性能似乎甚至优于从理论分析中得出的预期性能，这意味着存在进一步探索的途径。

本文的其余部分组织如下。第~2 节介绍了符号以及关于缩放和积和式的背景知识，第~3 节详细讨论了相关工作。第~4 节介绍了所提出的方法，并给出了二分图主算法的伪代码。扩展到一般无向图的情况在第~5 节中介绍。第~6 节展示了实验结果并与现有算法进行了比较。第~7 节对全文进行了总结。

\section*{2 符号与背景}

矩阵用粗体大写字母表示，例如 $\mathbf{A}$。我们用 $A_{ij}$ 表示通过删除矩阵 $A$ 的第 $i$ 行和第 $j$ 列得到的子矩阵。矩阵中的条目用小写字母和下标表示，例如 $a_{i,j}$ 表示矩阵 $A$ 在第 $i$ 行第 $j$ 列的元素。$A$ 的第 $i$ 行中非零元素的列标识表示为 $A(i,:)$。向量用粗体小写罗马字母表示，例如 $\mathbf{v}$。向量的分量用相同的字母和下标表示，例如 $v_i$。对于随机变量 $X$，我们用 $\mathbb{E}[X]$ 表示其期望。自然对数的底数用 $e$ 表示。

考虑我们要测量的某个量 $P$。在我们的案例中，$P$ 是积和式或

% ===== 第 4 页 =====
完美匹配的数量。假设我们可以访问一个无偏的随机过程（或更正式地称为估计量）$X$，使得 $\mathbb{E}[X] = P$。一种基于 $X$ 测量 $P$ 的技术是通过组合 $N$ 个 $X$ 副本的输出实现的。更具体地说，假设 $X_i$ 表示第 $i$ 个估计量的结果，则 $X' = (\sum_{i=1}^N X_i)/N$ 是 $P$ 的联合估计值。对于量 $P$ 的平均估计值 $X'$ 在满足 $\Pr(|X' - P| \leq \varepsilon P) \geq 1 - \delta$ 时达到 $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-近似。一般来说，通过模拟 $O\left( \frac{\mathbb{E}[X^2]}{\mathbb{E}[X]^2} \cdot \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2} \cdot \log\frac{1}{\delta} \right)$ 次试验可以实现 $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-近似。因此，比值 $\mathbb{E}[X^2]/\mathbb{E}[X]^2$ 被称为临界比，因为它是决定近似方案是否能在多项式时间内运行的关键因素。

一个 $n \times n$ 矩阵 $A \neq 0$ 被称为具有支撑，如果在其关联的二部图中存在一个完美匹配。此外，如果每个非零元素都能被置于至少一个完美匹配中，则该矩阵被称为具有全支撑。任何具有全支撑的非负矩阵 $A$ 都可以通过两个正对角矩阵 $R$ 和 $C$ 进行缩放，使得 $RAC$ 是双随机的（即，任意行和任意列的元素之和均为 $1$）。因此，具有全支撑的矩阵也称为可缩放矩阵。Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法 \cite{23} 是一种将矩阵缩放为双随机形式的著名方法。该算法通过交替归一化矩阵序列的列和行，生成一个矩阵序列（其极限是双随机的）。如果 $A$ 是对称且可缩放的，则 $S = RAR$ 是双随机的。虽然 Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法在极限情况下得到这个对称的双随机矩阵，但还有其他迭代算法在整个过程中保持对称性 \cite{17,18}。

如果一个 $n \times n$ 非负矩阵 $A$ 可通过正对角矩阵 $R$ 和 $C$ 缩放为双随机矩阵 $S = RAC$，那么函数
\[
g_A(x, y) = x^T A y - \sum_{i=1}^n \ln x_i - \sum_{j=1}^n \ln y_j \tag{1}
\]
在 $x = \operatorname{diag}(R)$ 和 $y = \operatorname{diag}(C)$ 处对正 $x$ 和 $y$ 达到最小值 \cite[命题~2]{14}。特别地，对于一个 $n \times n$ 的 $0$-$1$ 矩阵 $A$，我们有 $n \leq g_A(x, y) \leq n + n \ln n$，其中下界由置换矩阵达到，上界由全 $1$ 矩阵达到；在这两种情况下，$x^T A y = n$。

Idel \cite{12} 对计算双随机缩放问题的已知结果进行了全面综述。最近，对 Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法 \cite{3} 进行了更严格的分析，并提出了其他基于凸优化的高效算法 \cite{1,4}。

\section{相关工作}

Rasmussen \cite{22} 提出了一种实际高效的随机方法，用于估计 $0$-$1$ 矩阵的积和式，或用于计算二部图中的完美匹配数量。Rasmussen 算法访问矩阵的第一行，并在非零元素中均匀随机选择一个。然后从矩阵中移除第一行和所选非零元素所在的列，得到一个更小的矩阵。重复此过程，直到出现空行（此时返回零），或者原始矩阵的所有行都能选到一列（此时返回积和式 $X$ 的一个非零估计量）。该估计量是进行随机选择时第一行非零元素数量的乘积。尽管 Rasmussen 估计量在大多数情况下返回零，但它是一个无偏估计量，其期望值等于

% ===== 第 5 页 =====
永久量。Rasmussen 进一步证明，对于 $n\times n$ 矩阵 $A$，有 $\mathbb{E}[X^2] \leq \operatorname{Per}(A)^2 n!$，尽管可以将 $\operatorname{Per}(A)^2$ 简化为 $\operatorname{Per}(A)$。如第 2 节所述，$\mathbb{E}[X^2]$ 的值很重要，因为它表示了确保近似保证所需的样本数量。

我们的估计量 $X_A$ 遵循类似的思路。它也逐步生成完美匹配，但将均匀选择列替换为更有效的加权采样机制。采样中使用的权重通过一种用于将矩阵缩放为双随机形式的数值算法获得。

Beichland 和 Sullivan [2] 也研究了与我们相同的机制，并进行了一些初步分析。他们对 $\mathbb{E}[X^2]$ 的界限使用了一个符号，该符号表示所有完美匹配的选择概率的平均值。他们的分析很有价值，因为它表明缩放是有帮助的，但未能给出可计算的界限。我们在他们的工作基础上，提供了一些新的理论见解以及更详细的实验分析。更具体地说，我们提供了一种分析（主要结果见定理 2），该分析根据 $A$ 的缩放因子 $R$ 和 $C$ 给出了 $\mathbb{E}[X^2]$ 的可高效计算的界限。

对于估计一般无向图中完美匹配的数量，F\"urer 和 Kasiviswanathan [10] 讨论了三种随机算法，分别称为 Simple、REP 和 Greedy。其中称为 Simple 的算法是 Rasmussen 算法对图的直接改编，并以均匀概率选择邻居。REP 扩展了 Simple，使得在执行过程中的某些点，它会创建多个副本，每个副本选择自己的邻居，并且每个副本以类似方式继续执行。之后，每个副本的结果被合并。他们还讨论了针对二分图情况的类似算法 [9]。Greedy 试图通过以与节点度数减一成反比的概率选择每个节点来以更好的方式分配概率。F\"urer 和 Kasiviswanathan 得出结论：Simple 易于分析但最坏情况界限较高；Greedy 在许多图上表现良好但难以分析；而 REP 在随机（Erd\"os--R\'enyi）图上的性能具有最佳理论保证，尽管它在其他图上的最坏情况界限可能较高。我们的方法可以看作是 Greedy 的一个更复杂的变体。如果 Greedy 以等于邻居度数的概率选择随机邻居，那么它将等同于应用 Sinkhorn--Knopp 算法的一个步骤。然而，由于双随机缩放的全局最小化性质，我们变体的分析更简单，并揭示了更多见解，参见与双随机缩放相关的函数 (1)。

\textbf{4 所提出的算法及其分析}

在讨论我们的算法之前，我们首先说明在估计永久量时使用缩放的动机。以下引理突出了缩放因子与矩阵及其子矩阵的永久量之间的紧密联系。

\textbf{引理 1.} 设 $A$ 是一个具有完全支撑的 $n\times n$ $0$-$1$ 矩阵。设 $R$ 和 $C$ 是对角缩放矩阵，使得 $S = RAC$ 是一个双随机矩阵。那么，
\[
\operatorname{Per}(S) = \operatorname{Per}(A) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^n r_i \cdot c_i.
\]
此外，
\[
r_i \cdot c_j = \frac{\operatorname{Per}(A_{ij})}{\operatorname{Per}(A)} \cdot \frac{\operatorname{Per}(S)}{\operatorname{Per}(S_{ij})}.
\]

证明。由于$R$和$C$是对角矩阵，我们有$\operatorname{Per}(S) = \operatorname{Per}(A) \prod_i r_i \prod_j c_j$。等式$\operatorname{Per}(S_{ij}) = \operatorname{Per}(A_{ij}) \prod_{k \neq i} r_k \prod_{l \neq j} c_l$成立，因为$S_{ij}$中的所有对角乘积具有相同的值$\prod_{k \neq i} r_k \prod_{l \neq j} c_l$。将这两个等式逐边相除即得第二个结果。

\subsection*{4.1 算法}
用于估计积和式的算法如算法1所示。该算法输入一个$n \times n$的0-1矩阵$A$（其积和式非零），输出一个随机变量$X_a$和一个完美匹配（用于分析）。初始时$X_a$等于1。算法分$n$步进行。每一步中，算法向匹配中添加一个非零项，最终得到一个完美匹配。在第$i$步，从$A$的第$i$行中尚未被匹配的列中选择一个非零项。第$i$行选中的非零项定义了匹配的列。由于第$i$步中第$i$行是当前第一行，我们用$\sigma(i)$表示第$i$行选中的列，用$A^{(i)}$表示剩余的矩阵。非零项是根据剩余矩阵的双随机缩放版本中条目的值来选择的。随机变量$X_a$乘以所选非零项值的倒数。为了使算法有效，我们丢弃$A^{(i)}$中无法纳入完美匹配的非零项。这通过应用Dulmage-Mendelsohn \cite{8,21}分解，并过滤掉精细分解\cite{21}中落入非对角块中的条目来实现。

\textbf{算法1：积和式估计}
\begin{quote}
输入：$n \times n$的0-1矩阵$A$ \\
输出：积和式估计值$X_a$；完美匹配$\sigma$，其中第$i$个条目表示第$i$行选中的列。
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $X_a \leftarrow 1$
  \item $A^{(1)} \leftarrow A$
  \item \textbf{for} $i = 1$ \textbf{to} $n$ \textbf{do}
  \item \quad 过滤掉$A^{(i)}$中无法纳入完美匹配的条目
  \item \quad $[R^{(\sigma,i)}, C^{(\sigma,i)}] \leftarrow \text{Scale}(A^{(i)})$
  \item \quad 使用概率密度函数从$A^{(i)}(1,:)$中随机选择一个非零列$j$：
        \[ p_j = \frac{s_{1j}}{\sum_{k \in A^{(i)}(1,:)} s_{1k}}, \quad \text{对于所有非零项 } a^{(i)}_{1j} \]
        其中$s_{tk} = r_t^{(\sigma,i)} \cdot c_k^{(\sigma,i)}$是缩放矩阵$S = R^{(\sigma,i)} A^{(i)} C^{(\sigma,i)}$中的对应条目
  \item \quad $X_a \leftarrow X_a / p_j$
  \item \quad $A^{(i+1)} \leftarrow A^{(i)} \setminus \{\text{删除} A^{(i)} \text{的第一行和第} j \text{列}\}$
  \item \quad $\sigma(i) \leftarrow j$ \quad (假设使用原始编号)
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}

我们首先讨论算法的时间复杂度。算法共有$n$步，每一步需要计算一个矩阵的Dulmage-Mendelsohn分解，并对一个矩阵进行缩放。对于一个具有$m$个非零项的$n \times n$矩阵，这可以在$O(\sqrt{n} m)$时间内完成\cite{21}。缩放算法有多种；参见Idel的综述\cite{12}以及更近期的论文\cite{3,1,4}。基于凸优化技术的最新方法\cite{1,4}具有最小的运行时间复杂度$\tilde{O}(mn + n^{7/3})$和$\tilde{O}(m^{3/2})$——其中涉及与所需偏差的项。

Approximating the permanent is a well-studied problem. Valiant [26] showed the problem to
be #P-Complete. Jerrum et al. [13] discuss an approach using Markov Chains which can provide
an (1 + ε)-approximation for the permanent in fully polynomial time, with O˜(n10) complexity.
Their Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach makes use of the underlying graph being
bipartite, and the techniques cannot be generalized easily to the general graph case. Sˇtefankovic
et al. [24] take the MCMC approach and highlight the difficulties that arise. They also propose a
Markov Chain for efficiently estimating the number of perfect matchings in graphs from a special
class. Gurvits and Samorodnitsky [11] and Linial et al. [19] have used matrix scaling and proposed
deterministic approximations with exponential guarantees (2n and en respectively).
Rasmussen [22] proposes a practicallyefficient wayof estimatingthe permanent ofa 0-1matrix,
or the number of perfect matchings in bipartite graphs. This initial work is followed by a series of
others [2, 9, 10]. Rasmussen’s iterative algorithm uniformly and randomly chooses a nonzero from
the first row in the matrix at hand and discards the first row and the column of the chosen nonzero.
Thisstepisrepeateduntilthewholematrixisconsumedorthereisanemptyrowremaining. Inthe
former case, an estimate of a nonzero value is returned which is based on the number of nonzeros
of the first rows at each step; in the latter case zero is returned as an estimate.
We investigate an improvement of Rasmussen’s original approach in which edges are selected
non-uniformlybasedonamatrixscalingmethod,whichscalesamatrixtobedoublystochastic. We
provide an analysis of the stated approach by meticulously tracking the steps taken. The analysis

upper bounds the number of repetitions we must run to have quality guarantees on the estimated
permanent. To the best of our knowledge, for scaling-based permanent estimation, this work
presents the most thorough analysis in the literature with computable bounds. These ideas are also
extended to counting the number of perfect matchings in graphs. On the practical side, we present
an extensive set of experiments on a variety of random, constructed, and real-life instances, some
with known and others with unknown number of perfect matchings. Our experiments show that
the scaling-based selection mechanism exhibits a significantly better performance on all instances
comparedtotheknownmethods. Furthermore,thepracticalperformanceofouralgorithmseemsto
be even superior to the expected performance derived from our theoretical analysis, which implies
that there exist further avenues to explore.
The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 introduces the notation and the back-
ground on scaling and the permanent, and Section 3 discusses related work in detail. Section 4
introduces the proposed approach and presents the pseudocode of the main algorithm for bipartite
graphs. The extension to the general, undirected case is presented in Section 5. Section 6 presents
the experimental results and a comparison with existing algorithms. Section 7 concludes the paper.

3  Related  work
Rasmussen [22] proposes a practically efficient randomized approach for estimating the permanent
of a 0-1 matrix, or for counting perfect matchings in bipartite graphs. Rasmussen’s algorithm
visits the first row of a matrix and among the nonzeros, chooses one with uniform probability. The
first row and the column of the selected nonzero are then removed from the matrix and a smaller
matrix is obtained. This process is repeated until either there exists an empty row, in which case
zero is returned; or all rows of the original matrix were able to choose a column, in which case a
nonzero estimator of the permanent X is returned. This estimator is the product of the number
